lines:
Added a bounded per-user runtime baseline to `shell::environment` (the host-shell child environment): TEMP, TMP, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA on Windows; HOME, TMPDIR, TMP, TEMP elsewhere. An explicit invocation value still wins, and a launcher that defines no temp variable falls back to `std::env::temp_dir()`. This restores the scratch directory rustc/link.exe require (the LNK1104 against `C:\WINDOWS\lnk*.tmp`) and keeps `%TEMP%`/`%USERPROFILE%` expanded in cmd.exe instead of literal.

Scoped deliberately: `ProcessRunner::run_controlled` keeps its tested no-user-environment guarantee, so the baseline lives in the host-shell tool path (`shell_spec`), not in `prepare_command`. `host_network.rs` still asserts USERPROFILE is absent for that primitive.

Known boundary (not required for this defect): `python_spec` is unchanged because `python_adapter.rs:30` pins its environment, so host Python children still lack the baseline. Flagged as a possible follow-up.

No design element is bound to these files, so no design-model update was needed.

Verified: `cargo test -p aworkit-capability-host --no-fail-fast` exit 0, including the new `host_shell::host_shell_children_get_a_writable_user_temp_and_an_expanded_profile` and the unchanged `host_network::native_windows_launch_retains_system_root_without_inheriting_user_environment`; `cargo test --manifest-path desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib` 622 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.

Not verified: the running Aworkit process still uses the old code until it is rebuilt and restarted; the QA job 'Milestone 05' targets a Linux working directory (/home/timofl/src/Aworkit) and cannot run this Windows-only path here.

The controlled child environment in `crates/aworkit-capability-host/src/shell.rs` clears the environment and re-adds only `PATH` plus a machine-scoped Windows baseline (`WINDOWS_MACHINE_ENVIRONMENT`). It deliberately omits per-user variables, so every host command runs with `%TEMP%`, `%TMP%` and `%USERPROFILE%` undefined.

Consequences observed:
- `link.exe` (via rustc) resolves its scratch directory through TMP/TEMP and falls back to `C:\WINDOWS`, producing `LNK1104: cannot open file 'C:\WINDOWS\lnk{...}.tmp'`.
- Tools and tests that resolve the user home fail with `user home directory is unavailable`.
- `%TEMP%`/`%USERPROFILE%` command text stays literal in cmd.exe (the same class of defect the machine baseline already fixes for `%SystemDrive%`).

Fix: add a bounded, non-credential user baseline (TEMP, TMP, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH) to the controlled child environment, with a computed temp fallback when the launching process defines none. Explicit invocation environment still wins. Add a Windows regression test that a controlled child sees a non-empty, writable TEMP/TMP and an expanded USERPROFILE.

Out of scope: the other env_clear() sites (external agents, MCP peers, plugins, the sandboxed process runtime) keep their own allowlists.

data.title: Restore the per-user temp and profile variables in the controlled child environment
